On 18.04.2024, the Tribunal was informed that no witness was examined before Court Commissioner.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 12.
It is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi B h u t a n i ______________________________________________________________________ & Others., MAC APP. No. 550.2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1)
SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.

sentences.text: Now coming to the issue, it may be noted that in the present case, with respect to the accident which allegedly happened on 18.12.2020, no FIR was registered and the present DAR has been filed after conducting an investigation/ inquiry only on DD no.78A, dated 31.03.2021.
For the reasons best known to the parents of the petitioner, they did not get examined the injured child Sakshi before this Tribunal as a witness.

Any witness, though a minor but if, is capable of understanding the questions put and capable of giving rational answers to the same, is a competent witness and the petitioner being more than 11 years of age, was a competent witness.

In support of the claimant, only the mother of the injured, namely Smt. Vimla has been examined as PW1.
14.

In examination-in-chief Ex.PW1/A, PW1 has deposed about the manner in which the accident had taken place, however, in her cross- examination, PW1 has admitted that she was not an eyewitness of the accident.

Therefore, in view of her cross-examination, whatever has been deposed by PW1 regarding the manner of accident, is completely hearsay and the same could not be taken as proof of any fact related to the accident in question.

sentences.text: It is well-settled that the liability for damages caused by a motor vehicular accident has always been governed by the tort law principles.

As such, the liability of the respondents in the present claim petition is based on the proof of fault or at the least on the proof of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., the respondent no.1.

The Tribunal is not going into the question whether on 18.12.2020, it was the respondent no.1 who caused the accident of the petitioner/ injured by driving the offending vehicle rashly and/ or negligently as the respondents no.1 and 2 have not filed their written statement disputing all these facts and impliedly admitting that on the date of the accident the offending vehicle the owner of which was respondent no.2 and being driven by respondent no.1, was involved with which the injuries were caused to the petitioner.
Therefore, this Tribunal has to decide now whether the accident was caused due to sole rash and negligence of the respondent no.1 or the petitioner had also contributed in the happening of the accident.

16. As per the examination-in-chief (Ex.PW1/A) of the mother of the petitioner namely Smt. Vimla,
on the date of the accident i.e. 18.12.2020 at about 08:30 p.m., the petitioner Sakshi was playing outside the house in the Gali.

As per learned counsel for the petitioner, the house of the petitioner is situated in a congested area in which there is no park dedicated for playing of the children and if the children did not play on the road/ Gali, then where the children would play.

The argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner is not making logical sense that if there are no parks for the p l a y i n g  
o f ______________________________________________________________________ the children then the children would play on the road/ Gali which is primarily not meant for playing of the children but is meant for running of vehicles/ pedestrian.
If the petitioner was playing in the Gali on which vehicles used to run in case any accident would have happened, the petitioner would be liable for contributory negligence.
Accordingly, the contributory negligence of the petitioner is held as 50% in the facts and the circumstances of the present case.

17. In paragraph-2 of her affidavit Ex.PW1/A, the mother of the petitioner Smt. Vimla has clearly mentioned that the petitioner was playing outside of the Banjare Wali Gali and when the petitioner realised that in such a situation there would be contributing negligence of the minor petitioner and/or of her mother, who is a natural guardian of the petitioner, allowed her to play in the Gali.

The mother of the petitioner who was examined under section 168 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam on 01.08.2024 replied in negative to the query of the Tribunal if her daughter was playing on the road when the accident had happened.

It may also be mentioned that not only in the examination-in-chief but also in the cross-examination of the mother of the petitioner; PW1 deposed that, " It is correct that my minor daughter was playing on the road at the time of accident.

It is correct that on the road on which my daughter was playing at the time of accident has traffic and vehicles are plying on the road."
18. Merely because an accident may be, with a vehicle has occurred, there is no presumption in law or in fact that the accident happened because of the negligence of the driver in all and every case.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Minu B. Mehta (supra) held that the concept of owner's liability without any negligence is opposed to the basic principles of law.
The proof of negligence remains the linchpin to recover compensation.
The owner's liability arises out if his failure to discharge a duty cast upon him by law.

19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Minu B. Mehta (supra) further held that the right to receive compensation can only be against a person who is bound to compensate due to the failure to perform a legal obligation.
If a person is not liable legally, he is under no duty to compensate anyone else.
The Claims Tribunal is a Tribunal constituted by the State Government for expeditious disposal of the motor accident claims.
The general law applicable is only common law and the law of torts.

If under the law, a person becomes legally liable then the person suffering the injuries is entitled to be compensated and the Tribunal is authorised to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just.

The plea that the Claims Tribunal is entitled to award compensation which appears to be just when it is satisfied on proof of injury to a third party arising out of the use of a vehicle on a public place without proof of negligence if accepted would lead to strange results.

So,
before a person can be made liable to pay compensation for any injuries and damage which ______________________________________________________________________ have been caused by his action, it is necessary that the person injured or suffered damages should be able to establish that he has some cause of action against the party responsible.
Causes of action may arise out of actions for wrongs under the common law or for breaches of duties laid down by statutes.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Minu B. Mehta (supra) further held that in order to succeed in an action for negligence the plaintiff must prove (1) that the defendant had in the circumstances a duty to take care and that duty was owed by him to the plaintiff, and that (2) there was a breach of that duty and that as a result of the breach, damage was suffered by the plaintiff.
The master also becomes liable for the conduct of the servant when the servant is proved to have acted negligently in the course of his employment.
Apart from it, in common law the master is not liable as it is often said that the owner of a motor car does not become liable because of his owning a motor car.

21. The deposition of the sole witness examined on behalf of the petitioner i.e., the mother of the petitioner as PW1 does not prove the fact that in the accident which was caused by the respondent no.1, the same was caused because of rash and negligent act of the respondent no.1.

Though in the facts and circumstances of the case, the ratio decidendi of 'National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana, 2007 SCC OnLine Del 1700' is not applicable as in the present case, against the respondent no.1 being minor, no chargesheet was filed, however, inquiry against the minor was conducted on D D

ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 22.
On the basis of findings upon issue no.1 above, it is held that petitioner is entitled to get the compensation in this case.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 23. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.

"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding t h e  
c o m p e n s a t i o n .
 
T h i s ______________________________________________________________________ reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar,
(2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].

sentences.text: 24. The present claim petition pertains to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material losses.

So far non-pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e.
on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;

inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
"4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not b e e n ______________________________________________________________________ injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)

8 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life."
26.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 27.
PW1 Smt. Vimla, the only witness got examined on behalf of the petitioner, did not prove on record any medical bill with respect to the expenses incurred on treatment of her injured child Sakshi.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

______________________________________________________________________ Loss of earning during treatment:
28. PW1 has deposed that her daughter/ injured was studying in class IX in a Government School and due to injuries, she remained in bed for two months.
The Aadhaar Card of the injured child (Ex.PW1.2) shows her date of birth as 24.07.2007 and accordingly, on the date of accident on 18.12.2020, she was 13 years of age.
As the injured was admittedly a school going child, aged 13 years, she cannot be said to have suffered any loss of income during his treatment.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

Loss of Future Earnings :
29.

It is not the case of the petitioner that injuries suffered by her in the accident have resulted into any kind of permanent disability which may affect her future earnings and therefore, petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
30.

A perusal of the MLC bearing no. 9373, dated 18.12.2020, prepared at Dr. Hedgewar Hospital,
Delhi, which is part of the DAR Ex.PW1.1 (colly), reveals that in the accident, the petitioner suffered "fracture of shaft of right tibia and fibula ".

Treatment record shows that "CR (closed reduction) with Dar - Shakshi vs Yash And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35055930/

Accordingly, a total sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Attendant Charge:
31.

Though no documentary evidence has been led regarding hiring professional attendant during treatment, however, considering the nature of injury, it cannot be ignored that family members of the petitioner would have to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner in her routine activities and due to that their work/ job would definitely have suffered.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of the services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(Refer : DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Accordingly, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Pain & Sufferings:
32.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victims of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
______________________________________________________________________ 709.02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objective co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected Dar - Shakshi vs Yash And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35055930/
10 (c) Duration of the treatment."
33. In the instant case, as per MLC, the petitioner suffered fracture of both bone of right leg and the nature of injury was opined to be grievous in nature.

"CR (closed reduction) with cast application"
was done at hospital to treat the said fracture.
Her further treatment continued for about two months in the OPD of Dr. Hedgewar Hospital.

Keeping in view the nature of injury and the period of treatment, it can be safely inferred that the petitioner/ injured, who was a child aged 13 years at the time of accident, must have gone through immense pain and suffering during his treatment period and therefore, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation which is still based on a tortious liability.
It is well-settled that the liability for damages caused by a motor vehicular accident has always been governed by the tort law principles.
As such, the liability of the respondents in the present claim petition is based on the proof of fault or at the least on the proof of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., the respondent no.1.
The Tribunal is not going into the question whether on 18.12.2020, it was the respondent no.1 who caused the accident of the petitioner/ injured by driving the offending vehicle rashly and/ or negligently as the respondents no.1 and 2 have not filed their written statement disputing all these facts and impliedly admitting that on the date of the accident the offending vehicle the owner of which was respondent no.2 and being driven by respondent no.1, was involved with which the injuries were caused to the petitioner.
Therefore, this Tribunal has to decide now whether the accident was caused due to sole rash and negligence of the respondent no.1 or the petitioner had also contributed in the happening of the accident.
The Claims Tribunal is a Tribunal constituted by the State Government for expeditious disposal of the motor accident claims.
The general law applicable is only common law and the law of torts.
If under the law, a person becomes legally liable then the person suffering the injuries is entitled to be compensated and the Tribunal is authorised to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just.
Causes of action may arise out of actions for wrongs under the common law or for breaches of duties laid down by statutes.
The master also becomes liable for the conduct of the servant when the servant is proved to have acted negligently in the course of his employment.
Apart from it, in common law the master is not liable as it is often said that the owner of a motor car does not become liable because of his owning a motor car.
[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar,
(2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].
24. The present claim petition pertains to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of the services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
In the instant case, it cannot be inferred that after completion of the treatment, the petitioner would not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest as admittedly, the injuries sustained by her have not resulted into any kind of permanent disability.
Therefore, it is clear from the record that respondent no.1 being a minor, was driving the offending vehicle without holding driving license.
Respondent no.1 and 2 made no effort to rebut the said plea.
Thus, it stands established that respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the 'driver clause' of insurance policy Ex.R3W1/1.
40.
Law is well settled that in such a case, the insurance company would be primarily liable to pay compensation to third party/ claimant and it would be entitled to recover the paid compensation from the insured if it is proved that the insured was aware or had noticed that driver is not holding any driving license.
Reference can be made to the decision of Supreme Court given in case titled as United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Lehru & Ors., AIR 2003 SC 1292.
The respondent no.2 has not claimed his ignorance about absence of driving license or that his son (respondent no.1) had taken the offending vehicle without his authority.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the view that in order to serve the ends of justice in the facts and circumstances of this case, respondent no.3/ insurance company should be directed to pay the compensation and thereafter, it should recover the same from the owner and driver.
